newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom says board to discuss buyback.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says board to discuss buyback.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday that its board was due to discuss the possibility of a share repurchase programme at a meeting next Thursday.

"Telecom has for some time now publicly indicated that it is considering the possibility of share repurchases after reregistering under the 1993 Company's Act," the company said in response to a Stock Exchange inquiry about a strong rise in its share price.
"No final decision in this regard has yet been reached by the company, although the matter is due for discussion again at next week's board meeting on Thursday."
Telecom is due to publish its half year result on next Thursday.
It also said it had made inquiries of its major shareholders, Bell Atlantic and Ameritech about a news article on the possibility of one or both selling some or all of their shares.

It said Dermott Murphy, Vice President and Chief Financial officer of Bell Atlantic Enterprises International, responded that they have a policy of "not communicating on any acquisition or disposition...unless there is unusual trading activity".
Ameritech's Treasurer and Telecom Board Member, Rich Pehlke, responded "I am unaware of any such plans".
Telecom closed 16 cents higher at $7.62 on Thursday on volume of 1.87 million shares. Earlier they had traded as high as $7.70, an alltime high.

The company said its shares had risen overnight to the equivalent of NZ$7.58 on the New York Stock Exchange "primarily, as we understand it, due to buoyant conditions in U.S. markets following the outcome of the U.S. presidential election".
